title: Green peas, frozen, cooked with oil

content.title: About
content.content: Green peas are young pea pods harvested before the seeds fully mature. In frozen form they retain most of their nutrients, and cooking them with a small amount of oil adds flavor and improves nutrient absorption.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Frozen green peas are a convenient way to add vegetables to meals quickly.
Peas belong to the legume family and are a good source of plant protein.
Freezing preserves B‑vitamins and vitamin C, although some loss can occur during later heating.
Peas were domesticated more than 7,000 years ago in the Mediterranean region.
In several cultures green peas are a traditional dish for New Year celebrations.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: One cup of frozen peas provides about 8 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance and vegetarian diets.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes digestive health and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Peas contain folate, thiamine, and vitamin B6, which are important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids in peas help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Low in saturated fat and rich in potassium, peas contribute to normal blood pressure.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peas, ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared products often contain added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Legumes can cause bloating in sensitive individuals; increase portion size gradually.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Peas contain modest amounts of oxalates, which may be a concern for those prone to kidney stones.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat frozen peas with oil in a skillet, add them to soups, stews, salads, or serve as a side dish. They pair well with garlic, lemon, and fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen peas in the freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After thawing, use within 2–3 days and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
